common_name: Eburneo-Lowianum Cymbidium (Historic Primary Hybrid Boat Orchid)

planting.note: Repot back-bulb divisions into a coarse bark-based cymbidium mix in a wide, shallow pot; like both its parent species, this hybrid needs a distinct cool autumn night drop to reliably initiate winter-to-spring flower spikes.

directions: This primary hybrid between Cymbidium eburneum and Cymbidium lowianum combines the waxy, fragrant white flowers of eburneum with the larger size and longer, arching flower sprays of lowianum. Its chief historical significance is as a breeding parent: Sir George Holford crossed Cymbidium eburneo-lowianum with Cymbidium insigne in 1911 to raise the grex Cymbidium Alexanderi, whose spontaneous tetraploid 'Westonbirt' clone became a foundational ancestor of the large-flowered cymbidium hybrids widely sold today. Grow in bright, filtered light with a distinct cool snap in autumn to set spikes, watering freely while pseudobulbs are actively growing and allowing the mix to dry more once flowers appear. Repot only every two to three years, since cymbidiums bloom best when slightly pot-bound.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society International Orchid Register
